small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv2d 64→128, 3×3 on 128×128, batch 128) almost certainly dominates the 9.9 ms; further tuning of the InstanceNorm kernel will not move the needle. If staying small, add a few more autotune configs around BLOCK=4096/8192 with num_warps=8/num_stages=4 and consider vectorized float4 loads via tl.load on a reshaped pointer to improve memory throughput on the 16384-element rows.
- Fuse the divide-by constant into the conv bias path (bias_eff = bias) — actually the divide is already fused into the norm scale, so the only remaining tuning win is reducing the two-pass IO by using a single-pass Welford when HW fits in one block (HW=16384 fits BLOCK=16384, so skip the loop entirely and keep x in registers between pass 1 and pass 2).
- Use `num_stages=2` only (Ampere/Ada shared-mem pressure); pin `BLOCK=16384, num_warps=8` as the default for HW=16384 to remove autotune overhead.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit im2col gather, GEMM-K = IC*kh*kw = 576. Tile suggestion BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=3. Output is 128×128×126×126 ≈ 260M elements — this is where the time is.
- Fuse the entire InstanceNorm + divide as the conv epilogue is not viable (norm needs a full per-(N,C) reduction), so keep two kernels but make the conv write in channels-last layout so the norm reduction strides contiguously along HW. Alternatively, have the conv kernel additionally accumulate partial sum and sum-of-squares per (N,OC) into a workspace, then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/rstd and a third applies the affine — avoids re-reading the conv output for pass 1.
- For the norm itself, switch to one program per (N,C) with a persistent kernel: HW=15876 (126*126) fits a single 16384-BLOCK load, so do Welford in registers in a single pass and write out in the same kernel — eliminates the second global read of x.
